red.focus: Research legal rights without making promises
red.summary: A client may describe a serious injustice, but research must identify the governing protection and its limits. Learn to connect a personal story with the right legal source.
checklist: I can find a source protecting an asserted interest
I can record the claimant and alleged duty holder
I can identify the basic remedy and forum

sections.title: Translate Concern Into a Search Question
sections.body_md: A client says an employer shared a medical record without permission. The first research question is not whether all privacy invasions are illegal. Identify the country, employer type, information shared, recipient and date. Then find any relevant data-protection, confidentiality, employment or constitutional rules. A right is useful only when its source, scope and conditions are known. A disciplined search avoids giving emotionally reassuring but legally unsupported advice.

sections.title: Check the Defendant and Protected Person
sections.body_md: A rule may protect patients against health providers, public employees against agencies, or consumers against particular companies. Its definition of protected person and regulated actor can determine the entire case. Before quoting a broad statement of rights, read those definitions. The same incident may engage several sources with different conditions. A beginner's source note should identify the rights holder, duty holder, triggering conduct and legally available response.

sections.title: Rights Need an Accessible Route
sections.body_md: A right can be enforced through an agency complaint, civil claim, employment tribunal or constitutional procedure depending on the jurisdiction. Some routes require exhaustion, notice or deadlines. The client should know what practical step is available and when action must be taken. Research that stops at an elegant declaration can fail the person seeking help. Good advice connects the legal protection with the institution able to provide meaningful relief.

yellow.focus: Trace exceptions and statutory definitions in rights research
yellow.summary: Develop research methods that test the entire right, not just its opening language. Learn to find regulatory guidance and exceptions without mistaking them for higher authority.
checklist: I can find legislative definitions and exceptions
I can check authoritative guidance against binding text
I can explain when consent or public interest matters

sections.title: A Protection Often Has Conditions
sections.body_md: A data-protection rule may permit disclosure under a defined legal obligation or medical emergency while prohibiting unrelated sharing. To research the claim, follow the statutory provision to its definitions, exceptions and enforcement sections. An introductory summary may omit critical qualifications. Read cross-references and any implementing regulations. The question becomes whether this particular disclosure met the legal conditions, not whether medical data deserves protection in the abstract.

sections.title: Guidance Is Not Always Law
sections.body_md: An agency may publish useful guidance explaining its interpretation of a statute. Such material may be important, but its legal status differs by jurisdiction and context. A lawyer should separate binding regulations, official interpretive statements and general educational advice. Where guidance appears inconsistent with statutory text or precedent, identify which source has legal priority. This approach helps students use practical research tools without substituting convenient summaries for governing authority.

sections.title: Negative and Positive Evidence
sections.body_md: A client's account may support an unauthorized disclosure, while a signed consent form or statutory duty could matter to exceptions. A balanced search identifies evidence for both sides. Do not assume that a document labeled consent necessarily meets the legal test; scope, timing and capacity may be relevant. The research product should state which facts determine whether the exception applies and what additional evidence is needed. This makes the final advice both concise and reliable.

orange.focus: Research overlapping constitutional and statutory rights
orange.summary: Handle disputes in which several legal frameworks protect related interests. Distinguish which source controls which defendant, what remedy follows and what must be proved.
checklist: I can map overlapping legal protections without double counting
I can identify vertical and horizontal application
I can compare procedural routes and exhaustion requirements

sections.title: One Event, Several Bodies of Law
sections.body_md: A public university records a student's private communications and shares them with a contractor. Constitutional principles, administrative law, privacy legislation and contract terms may each bear on the event. A sophisticated researcher does not assume they create identical claims. Make a table: source, actor bound, protected interest, conditions, exceptions and remedy. Then test whether the university's status or the contractor's role changes the available route. The map makes overlapping protection intelligible.

sections.title: Rights Against Public and Private Actors
sections.body_md: Constitutional restrictions often operate differently against the state than against private persons, though legal systems vary. Privacy legislation may reach organizations that constitutional rights do not directly govern. A researcher must determine the defendant's legal status and the jurisdiction's approach to horizontal effect. A decision from another country can illustrate a method but is not automatically controlling. Avoid imposing one system's classification on another's constitutional structure.

sections.title: Procedure Is Part of the Protection
sections.body_md: A person may need to complain to a regulator, satisfy an exhaustion rule, or seek urgent interim relief before a full claim. Those conditions can determine whether a seemingly strong right produces a timely remedy. The research memo should identify deadlines, available review, and enforcement powers. Technical accuracy and humane advice meet here: a student who finds the right but misses the remedy pathway may leave the client unprotected despite excellent theoretical knowledge.

black.focus: Audit human-rights claims for legal force and practical protection
black.summary: At doctoral depth, research rights that cross constitutional, regional and international legal systems. Develop evidence-sensitive advice without confusing influential declarations with directly enforceable obligations.
checklist: I can distinguish treaty obligations from domestic remedies
I can audit binding force and reservations
I can analyze whose access to rights enforcement is missing

sections.title: The International Source Problem
sections.body_md: A human-rights declaration can express a powerful universal standard while not itself creating a domestic cause of action everywhere. Treaties may bind ratifying states, but domestic enforcement can depend on incorporation, jurisdiction, reservations and available remedies. A legal researcher must identify each instrument's status, the relevant state's commitments, and the institution able to hear a claim. Conflating moral authority with a specific court's legal power can mislead those facing serious threats to liberty or safety.

sections.title: Investigate Institutional Obstacles
sections.body_md: A person may formally hold a right but lack legal aid, translation, safe access to proceedings or a realistic route to enforce a judgment. Research should include procedure and institutions alongside substantive norms. Reports by rights bodies can supply context or evidence, but their legal effect varies. The advanced lawyer distinguishes an adjudicative finding, authoritative interpretation, scholarly opinion and advocacy report. That classification protects both the claimant and the integrity of the legal argument.

sections.title: Write Rights Advice With Precision
sections.body_md: A doctoral memorandum should state exactly which legal instruments apply, why, and what remains disputed. It should record primary sources in authoritative languages, the status of any domestic implementing law, and available review or urgent protections. Where the law fails vulnerable people, identify reform arguments separately from existing remedies. The final measure of research quality is whether it helps a person make an informed choice about protecting their dignity and freedom, not how many instruments the bibliography contains.
